documents.title: Joint Report from Bureau of Street Services and Department of Transportation
documents.excerpt: FORM GEN. 160 (Rev. 8-12) CITY OF LOS ANGELES INTER-DEPARTMENTAL CORRESPONDENCE DATE: August 7, 2026 TO: The Honorable City Council FROM: Keith Mozee for Executive Director and General Manager Bureau of Street Services (StreetsLA) Laura Rubio-Cornejo General Manager Department of Transportation (LADOT) SUBJECT: STREET SWEEPING AND PARKING ENFORCEMENT (CF 24-1219-S1) RECOMMENDATION That the City Council note and file this report, as it is provided for informational purposes only. SUMMARY Pursuant to the recommendations adopted by the City Council on August 29, 2025 (Council File 24-1219-S1), this report provides information in response to the following recommendations: • Current coordination efforts between street sweeping and parking enforcement operations on posted routes. • Recommendations to improve interdepartmental collaboration to facilitate simultaneous parking enforcement and street sweeping, including resources needed for implementation. • Explore potential technology or equipment that could be utilized to support operations. • Data on citations issued for street sweeping, including information on disputed citations issued in areas where street sweeping did not take place. • Develop policies that would prevent the issuance of parking citations in areas where posted street sweeping does not occur and after street sweepers have passed. DISCUSSION StreetsLA is responsible for maintaining one of the largest municipal street networks in the nation, including 1,384 total street sweeping routes, accounting for 13,891 curb miles of public streets. The purpose of the street sweeping program (Program) is to prevent debris from washing into storm drains, waterways, and ultimately the ocean. It also serves to maintain clean and safe streets for residents and visitors by removing debris that can cause accidents or block storm drains, and helps to improve the overall aesthetics of neighborhoods. The Program is organized into three major types of routes: • Posted Routes - Comprising 34% of all City streets, posted routes are primarily residential streets with signs detailing parking restrictions on days/times that street sweeping is scheduled to occur. The installation of the parking restriction signage, and enforcement of The Honorable City Council August 7, 2026 Page 2 of 3 those restrictions are the responsibility of LADOT. In the current fiscal year, posted routes are swept bi-weekly. • Commercial Corridors - Comprising 11% of City streets, these routes are heavily trafficked commercial corridors that are swept before the morning commute. In the current fiscal year, commercial corridors are swept every three-four weeks. • Open Routes - Comprising 55% of City streets, these streets are not regularly scheduled for sweeping, and do not have posted parking restrictions.
